vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: sql-generator
Version: 2.3.1

The SQL Generator skill is a template-based tool designed to output SQL snippets for common database tasks such as table creation, querying, and indexing. The core logic in `scripts/sql.sh` uses simple keyword matching and heredocs to generate static SQL text based on user input, without executing commands against a live database or performing any high-risk system operations.

llm.summary: The skill's files and runtime instructions are coherent with its stated purpose (generating and explaining SQL); it includes a local shell script that templates DDL/queries and does not request credentials, installs, or network access in the provided content.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (SQL generation, explainer, DDL, mock data, migration) align with the included artifacts: SKILL.md describing commands and a bash script (scripts/sql.sh) that generates SQL. No unrelated credentials, binaries, or config paths are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md simply exposes SQL-related commands and example usage; it does not instruct the agent to read arbitrary host files, access environment secrets, or send data externally. The script content shown generates templated SQL and prints to stdout.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only skill with an included script). No downloads or package installs are declared, so nothing new would be written to disk beyond the shipped files.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials. The provided script uses only standard POSIX utilities (date, tr, cat) and templates SQL; it does not access secrets or external services in the visible portion.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill is user-invocable (normal). The skill does not request system-wide changes or persistent privileges in the provided materials.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears internally consistent and limited to generating SQL templates. Before installing or running it: (1) review the full scripts/sql.sh file (the manifest shows a truncated excerpt) to confirm there are no hidden network calls, credential access, or code that executes commands against live systems; (2) run the script in a sandbox or non-production environment first; (3) never run generated SQL on production databases without human review; (4) if you plan to add DB connectivity later, require only the specific database credentials needed and avoid giving broad cloud or system credentials.
